notes.title: Lewis Carroll and Studio Ghibli: How Catie in MeowmeowLand Came to Life
notes.content:
Cats prowl through the history of fiction, lending their feline mischief to countless classic works. Glimpses of gleaming eyes and the rumble of gentle purrs are everywhere, as the little furry companions wriggle their way into novels, movies, and games. The upcoming [i]Catie in MeowmeowLand[/i] is a whimsical journey through a mystical feline world, and has its roots in the many cat-centric creations of the past.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39294251/2c69c0778440b01175ca6a421d44985fc0f77d3a.png[/img]

[h2]Tumbling Down the Rabbithole[/h2]

The year is 1865 and London is the most populous city in the world. The River Thames bristles with sailing barges and rowing boats, drifting in the shadows of hulking half-constructed steamships. In the newly-built London Underground, locomotives propel wooden cars through dark tunnels, gas lamps lighting the way.

It is the year that Britain’s first speed limit is put in place, outlawing blistering speeds of 2 mph in town and 4 mph in the country. Elsewhere in the world, the New York Stock Exchange establishes its first permanent headquarters in New York City. Within a year, dynamite will be invented. Transatlantic telegraph cables have failed once, but will succeed in a years’ time. Wars rage and nations are reshaped.

And in London, the bustling hub of a changing world, a man by the name of Lewis Carroll publishes a timeless piece of children’s fiction, [i]Alice’s Adventures in Wonderland[/i].

One of the best-known pieces of Victorian literature, Carroll’s novel is a classic which virtually everyone alive knows of, and has likely read or experienced through one of its many adaptations. The beautifully written tale of fantastical adventure brings to life enchantingly odd characters and imagery - unique creations that ensnare the imagination and embed deep in memory. Figures like the Mad Hatter, White Rabbit, and Cheshire Cat remain cultural touchstones to this day, and have endlessly influenced the fantasy genre and wider popular culture. The fantastic world of Wonderland, with all its absurd eccentricities, is one which generation after generation of children yearn to visit.

The timelessness of this tale has led to countless adaptations. The 1951 film, [i]Alice in Wonderland[/i], was Walt Disney’s 13th animated feature film, and received a surprisingly lackluster initial reception. A considerably more successful 1974 theater re-release cemented its popularity, and in more recent years Disney released the Tim Burton-directed live-action adaptation. Both movies depict the classic tale of Alice falling into the bizarre and lore-rich world of Wonderland, discovering its countless peculiar creatures and characters. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39294251/5e2dc67e03bdd8ff69e151379bb65b08ddaf13d1.png[/img]

[h2]The Magic of Studio Ghibli[/h2]

Over a century patters by. The year is 1985, or Showa 60 in the Japanese calendar, a time of economic prosperity for the country. Japan is about to host the 1985 Summer Universiade in Kobe, as well as Miss International 1985 in the city of Tsukuba. A group of creatives fresh off the success of the 1984 film [i]Nausicaä of the Valley of the Wind[/i] join together to found an animation film studio. The legendary Studio Ghibli is born, and founders Hayao Miyazaki, Toshio Suzuki and Isao Takahata begin work on the magical films that will inspire a whole new generation.

In just a few years, one of their most acclaimed and iconic films will arrive, in [i]My Neighbour Totoro[/i], the story of two young girls discovering a supernatural world of woodland spirits and wondrous creatures. One of the most striking elements is the Catbus, the gigantic flying cat with headlights for eyes, windows running along its side, and a hollow interior with fur-covered seats. This wondrously bizarre creation ferries characters to and fro, all the while wearing a wide grin uncannily reminiscent of Carroll’s Cheshire Cat.

Many years and incredible animated creations later, 2002 delivers Studio Ghibli’s [i]The Cat Returns[/i], telling the story of a girl with a feline affinity. Able to speak the language of cats, she crosses paths with a Prince of the Cat Kingdom, and finds herself invited to his realm. She explores a world filled with absurd and whimsical cat characters, and all the spell-binding strangeness Studio Ghibli is known for.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39294251/81f5fbbd960e6946fa961dc82f0e0dd8db2cc3d1.png[/img]

[h2]The Wonders of MeowmeowLand[/h2]

The common ingredients of these creations, separated by continents, oceans, and over a century, are manifold - but they will soon share yet another connection. The upcoming fantastical adventure game, [i]Catie in MeowmeowLand[/i], draws upon the rich shared elements of both. It is a love letter and homage to the peculiar creatures and characters of [i]Alice’s Adventures in Wonderland[/i], and the fantastical lore-rich worlds of Studio Ghibli.

References to Carroll’s work abound - from a fateful tumble down an animal’s burrow to the appearance of a highly familiar sentient egg, and a furry creature leading the way with a time-piece in its grip. Studio Ghibli fans will feel the thrill of recognition as well - in the creature somewhere between cat and train which carries Catie on her journey, and the wondrous world bursting with eccentric feline characters of every persuasion.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39294251/cf7fa2b5707e4b414abefbb068968931b1f20b69.png[/img]

However, there is a deeper similarity which unifies all of these stories, a common essence that binds them together. A human discovering a world of magic, filled with imaginary creatures. A rich, fantastical world bursting with life, with unique details and characters, and eccentricities waiting around each and every corner. It is about discovering a hole in the reality of the ordinary world, and plunging through it into a spectacular realm of dazzling imagination, of joyous whimsy, and most importantly, of cats.


[i]Catie in MeowmeowLand[/i] is a traditional point-and-click adventure game set in a bizarre world of cats and ludicrous characters. Echoing the adventures of Alice, Catie follows a white cat with a pocket clock into her garden, and is swept down a rabbit hole into the world of MeowmeowLand. From there, your task is to solve puzzles and help Catie get back home!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39294251/257cb1ed3e2f4477af41f6ded727eba6f12cad65.png[/img]

Find your way through the strange land of MeowmeowLand, meeting a host of peculiar characters and solving a series of bizarre and original puzzles that will test your imagination. Sink into a hand-crafted, detailed world, with original music, 24 2D hand-drawn sceneries, and over 100 uniquely amusing characters with individual voices and over 2 hours of animations.

[b]Catie in MeowmeowLand[/b] is available now on Steam, alongside Nintendo Switch, PlayStation 5, PlayStation 4, Xbox Series X|S, Xbox One and GOG!

notes.title: Catie in MeowmeowLand Now Available in Hungarian & Czech!
notes.content:
Hello Cat Lovers!

We’ve been overwhelmed by the positive love and reception for Catie’s release! Thank you all so much for your support of the weird and wonderful!

We are super proud to announce that Catie in MeowmeowLand will now support Hungarian and Czech languages!

In addition to that, we have also altered many levels to incorporate more hints and aid player direction.

That’s all for now! Please enjoy Catie in Meowmeowland, and tag us on our social media! We’d love to see it.

notes.title: Catie in MeowMeowLand: The Big Adventure Event Showcase
notes.content:
Dive right into a world of wonder and mischief with the ARTillery Dev Team, the creators of Catie in MeowMeowLand! 

Set in an alternate, trip-inducing Alice in Wonderland setting, you will find yourself surrounded by beautiful, bizarre art and thinking unconventionally in order to continue on. Immerse yourself in a strange kind of nostalgia with homages to your favourite rhymes and childhood figures, as well as the familiar “follow the white rabbit” leading you onward. 

The dev team will be leading you through and explaining their processes all the while! You will meet [b]Marek Hlavaty[/b], the Head Developer & Art Director from ARTillery, as well as his associate, [b]Natalia Kratochvila[/b]!

Catie in MeowMeowLand: The Big Adventure Event Showcase will occur on [b]Friday, 21st Jan at 9:00 PM PDT[/b] / [b]Saturday, 22nd Jan at 6:00 AM CET[/b]!
